query: Some virtual machines stop responding, and applications experience reduced capacity while recovery attempts fail.
Requests between services are timing out, and multiple applications are losing connectivity following a network change.
Some user requests return server errors after a caching configuration change, while most other requests continue working.
A live application suddenly shows missing records across hundreds of user-created scoreboards following a destructive storage operation.
Several monitoring features become slow or unavailable, including web requests, log access, and network metrics, following a disruption in internal communications.
Automated build jobs stop processing, and a large queue of pending tasks continues to grow after a recent infrastructure change.
Servers in one region cannot look up any hostnames after a config update to the internal name servers, though direct IP connections still work.
Work sits waiting and never starts right after we deployed a database field type change, and rolling back made it worse.
The dashboard will not load and no new pipelines can start, with cross-origin errors between the frontend and the API after a security rule change.
Traffic across about half of our network dropped within minutes after a router config tweak aimed at easing congestion, and many cities went dark.
Roughly twenty busy data centers fell off the network at once after a routing change meant to improve resilience.
Authentication tokens for automated services suddenly stopped being accepted after a release that added a last-used timestamp, breaking several internal products.
A public resolver started returning SERVFAIL for valid domains for hours after a refresh of the root zone data.
Edge proxies across the fleet start failing and users see error pages, shortly after a database permissions change, and at first it looks like an attack.
A large share of HTTP requests return 500 errors for about half an hour after a firewall body-parsing change rolled out to counter a framework vulnerability.
All writes to object storage fail and a third of reads fail globally after we rotated storage credentials.
Our desktop browser hangs for nearly two hours worldwide after a cloud load balancer silently started offering a newer protocol version.
All sites become unreachable for under an hour after we restricted which hosts could send and receive name server traffic to defend against amplification attacks.
Every logged-in product refuses requests for about twenty-five minutes after an internal system generated a bad configuration and pushed it out.
All links shown by the engine carry a malware warning for roughly forty minutes after a blocklist update was pushed.
Visitors hitting our global HTTPS load balancer get 404 pages for any URL until the last known good configuration was restored.
Batch and transfer traffic is slow across several regions for most of a day after a network control plane config rollout, while user-facing traffic is fine.
Pushing code over git suddenly fails for all users right after we deployed the git server and old instances were being retired.
Package requests all return 403 Forbidden and the CDN is hammered by retries after we simplified the caching layer config.
Water treatment plant chemical feed ran far above its normal rate for hours after an operator keystroke, and a lead operator did not act on the high reading.
All our sites drop for about six minutes after a firewall rule change on the load balancers blocked return traffic.
Mac jobs pile up in a growing backlog and keep getting requeued while the virtualization cleanup service misbehaves.
Linux VM jobs fail to boot because the base disks they depend on are gone after an automated cleanup service ran.
Many jobs fail or hang on autoscaled hosts after we rolled out a new worker version, and a rollback was needed.
A whole availability zone loses compute instances and disk volumes after a storm knocked out the utility feed and backup generators did not take over.
API success rate dips to about 75 percent and the dashboard is dozens of times slower, even though redundant switch pairs and databases seem healthy.
Customers cannot change settings or view logs for two days after a leased data center lost power and failover to the backup site was only partial.
Alarm software silently fails in a utility control room, operators do not notice overloaded lines, and failures cascade across a huge region.
Site returns 503 pages for two hours after a brief power disruption reboots a quarter of servers, and our chat-based ops tooling is down too.
A small share of persistent disks in one zone return sporadic I/O errors for days and snapshots fail, with rare permanent data loss.
Background job writes fail for about ten percent of requests and queues back up after we added new coordination-service hosts too quickly during an upgrade.
Brief intermittent packet loss between many cloud regions for twenty minutes that cleared on its own through automatic mitigation.
Customers see reference numbers on new tickets leap ahead unexpectedly, such as 52 for an account with only twenty, from a Postgres sequence.
Right at the year rollover, some DNS answers for aliased names fail on a handful of machines, and a counter went negative.
Virtual machines, websites and other products built on blob data all slow down or fail at once, shortly after we started rolling out a performance tweak.
Some IPv6 traffic sees heavy packet loss and added latency for about 25 minutes after an automated policy change on one router in a single city.
Every switching node on our research backbone grinds to a halt for hours and traffic barely moves after some strange messages started circulating.
Players worldwide cannot log in or open the store for two hours, with API probes timing out from over half of our test locations and packet loss rising.
Our admin web console and many management APIs return 5xx errors, and the authorization backend keeps falling over after a new frontend release and a backend update.
Object storage requests show about 20 percent errors for four hours, and mail, photos and file-sharing products built on top also get error spikes.
All of our apps and internal tools disappear from the internet, including the ones engineers need to fix it, right after a routine backbone maintenance command.
Many edge products return 401 Unauthorized for key-value reads and writes for about 35 minutes, right after a deployment tool configuration change.
A key facility in the Portland area goes offline for hours after the utility did maintenance, and a ground fault and failed breakers stop it coming back.
Applications in our busiest US hosting area cannot open new database connections overnight, then load balancer health checks fail and new virtual machines will not launch.
Newly created virtual machines, VPN tunnels and network load balancers are unreachable on their public addresses for about two hours, while existing ones are fine.
Our own website and all customer sites on one file store throw errors, scheduled tasks stop running, and recovery takes hours even though the data is mirrored.
Our main API gets a burst of 5xx errors for under two minutes, then replicas stop syncing with duplicate key errors, so we move reads to the primary.
After the new game release some players' Windows PCs refuse to start up, because the graphics content upgrade removed a startup file from the system drive.
Every web and API request fails for about 36 minutes right after a database config change made health checks to the read replicas fail.
Several managed products in Europe return errors for under two hours because the front-end load balancing layer is failing.
Virtual machines in every region lose their external connectivity for about 18 minutes, with inbound internet traffic not reaching them.
The site goes down for hours during planned switch software upgrades, with servers losing the paired network switches and a messy recovery.
A customer's entire private virtualization environment across two zones disappears after a provisioning run, and only backups held elsewhere let them recover.
Many managed products in London show elevated errors and latency for more than a day, even though they were designed to survive a single zone failing.
About 2 percent of CDN requests get generic error pages and tail latency triples, with one process stuck in a loop after a new DDoS rule.
Our payments API stops answering for roughly 15 seconds during a planned schema change that we thought was safe.
Pages show stale or inconsistent data and webhooks stop delivering for a full day after a brief connectivity blip between data centers.
